newsitem.title: UK: UK gas shippers protest against Network Code change.
newsitem.headline: UK gas shippers protest against Network Code change.

text.p: Gas shippers in Britain are expressing concern over the latest modification to the Network Code, the rule book governing gas trade and use of the trunk pipeline system, industry sources said.
Modification 117, which relates to capacity reservation on the interconnector pipeline between Scotland and Northern Ireland, is the bone of contention.
The clause will introduce "contract carriage" instead of "common carriage", and could have implications for the Bacton-Zeebrugge pipeline when it opens in October 1998.

Gas shippers who do not want to be identified claim that some of their number, who have already booked space on the Northern Ireland link, are seeking to block National Transmission System (NTS) operator TransCo, from selling extra capacity on the line.
The result of their plea to TransCo has been 117, now up for consideration by industry regulator Ofgas.
At present, the NTS operates on "common carriage", meaning any shipper can ask for capacity and if too many apply, all will have their volumes prorated downwards.
But if 117 is accepted, shippers asking for extra capacity will be told none is available under "contract carriage", as prorating will no longer apply.

"It will be the only bit of contract carriage on the NTS," said a shipper. "We're not against contract carriage in principle, but we don't want it introduced piecemeal. We feel that TransCo is coming under pressure from narrow interest groups."
Representations to TransCo on the modification must be in by 1700 GMT on Tuesday. TransCo must then pass them on to Ofgas by Friday.
"Ofgas is aware of the urgency of this modification and anticipates a decision on Monday 24 February. However Ofgas has reservations about the scope of this modification," an Ofgas spokesman said.
